summary: Found several documentation claims that do not match the implementation, including a non-existent backend class, incorrect request header behavior, an invalid proxy usage example, an incorrect trace event name, and overstated proxy/HTTP-version limitations.

findings.title: Proxy example calls request() on httpcore.Proxy, which has no request method
findings.evidence: docs/proxies.md shows `r = proxy.request("GET", "https://www.example.com/")`, but httpcore.Proxy only stores url, headers, ssl_context, and auth; request handling is performed by ConnectionPool/AsyncConnectionPool.
findings.suggested_fix: Change the example to use the pool: `r = pool.request("GET", "https://www.example.com/")`.
findings.verification_notes: Confirmed: docs/proxies.md calls proxy.request(...) but httpcore.Proxy is a config model without request(); ConnectionPool.request is the correct API.

findings.title: Direct Request construction is documented as automatically adding a Host header
findings.evidence: The docs show `httpcore.Request("GET", "https://www.example.com/", headers=headers)` producing a Host header, but Request.__init__ only enforces supplied headers. Host is added later by include_request_headers in the pool/interface request path.
findings.suggested_fix: Clarify that Host is added by connection pools/interfaces, not by Request itself, or update the example to reflect supplied headers only.
findings.verification_notes: Confirmed: Request("GET", url).headers is [] at construct time; Host is added later by include_request_headers(). Docs show Host present immediately.

findings.title: Documentation references httpcore.backends.asyncio.AsyncioBackend, which does not exist
findings.evidence: The docs list `httpcore.backends.asyncio.AsyncioBackend`, but the repository provides `httpcore.AnyIOBackend` (implemented in httpcore/_backends/anyio.py) and no asyncio backend module.
findings.verification_notes: Confirmed: docs/table-of-contents.md lists httpcore.backends.asyncio.AsyncioBackend; no such module. Actual async backend is httpcore.AnyIOBackend (httpcore/_backends/anyio.py).

findings.title: Trace event list uses http11.receive_response, but code emits receive_response_headers
findings.evidence: docs/extensions.md lists `"http11.receive_response"`, while the implementation traces `"receive_response_headers"` and `"receive_response_body"`.
findings.suggested_fix: Update the documented HTTP/1.1 trace event names to match the implementation.
findings.verification_notes: Confirmed: docs/extensions.md event list includes "http11.receive_response"; implementation traces receive_response_headers / receive_response_body.

findings.title: Docs say proxies only support HTTP/1.1 servers, but tunnel connections can negotiate HTTP/2
findings.evidence: docs/proxies.md states that httpcore only supports proxies to HTTP/1.1 servers, but AsyncTunnelHTTPConnection/ TunnelHTTPConnection can create an HTTP/2 connection when ALPN negotiates h2.
findings.suggested_fix: Clarify that the proxy connection itself is HTTP/1.1 while tunneled remote connections may use HTTP/2 when supported.
findings.verification_notes: Confirmed: docs/proxies.md says proxies only support HTTP/1.1 servers; TunnelHTTPConnection can negotiate h2 via ALPN when http2=True.
